cap.backendHint: Read existing probe results without starting an extra probe.
cap.credentialsRequired: Enter the node and sharing secrets before exporting a runnable configuration.
cap.default: Not overridden; the owning component uses its default.
cap.deploymentHint: Generate agent and visitor configurations and review host commands.
cap.diagnosticsHint: Runtime observations from the server and connected agents. Refresh to obtain a new snapshot.
cap.hostOperations: Commands to run on the device (advanced)
cap.hostOperationsHint: Commands are generated for review and are never executed by the console. Adapt service scope and filesystem paths to the target host.
cap.localAuthority: This page generates a device configuration file. Changes are not sent automatically; local resource permissions are controlled by the file on that device.
cap.noLogs: No log file is configured. Read stderr through your service or container manager.
cap.notProbing: No active health check. Backends are assumed available until a probe says otherwise.
cap.operationsManual: Use the operating guide for Docker, verified binary updates and transparent proxy kernel rules. Those operations run on the host.
cap.peersHint: Latest 512 observations in this forwarding generation. Entries describe events, not a permanent session inventory.
cap.restartInstructions: Stop the server before replacing files. Back up the active runtime snapshot: {path}. Place felucca-runtime-restart.json at the snapshot path used on the next start (including any --runtime-config override). Place felucca-server-restart.json at the startup configuration path. Keep existing traffic and platform journals. Restrict both files to the service account. Run --check with the same paths, then restart. Restore the backups if startup fails. Never overwrite a live snapshot.
cap.restartRequired: Valid configuration; these changes require a process restart.
cap.tokenHint: The old token will stop working. A newly generated token is downloaded only after saving; store it securely.
cap.truncated: Showing a bounded recent window; older or excess entries are omitted.
cap.unavailable: Unavailable: the node may be offline, the tunnel inactive, or the agent may need upgrading.
cap.uploadHint: Select PEM files. Uploaded paths are placed in the draft; save the configuration to activate them.
cert.issuance_failed: Issuance failed; inspect the server log
chart.noData: This host does not provide this data yet
chart.seriesDescription: {name} time series: left and right arrows step through samples, Home and End jump to the first and last, Escape returns to live
config.applyMessage: Forwarding services reload and existing connections are interrupted.
config.description: Validate, import and manage the whole server configuration.
config.exportMessage: The file contains node keys and other credentials. Keep it somewhere safe.
config.footerHint: Validate a change before applying it to the service.
config.importTooLarge: A configuration file cannot exceed 2 MiB.
config.imported: File loaded. Validate it before saving.
config.info: Choose a feature and review its purpose and defaults. Before saving, validation explains how changes take effect. Untouched keys keep their values.
config.title: Server settings
dialog.editor.advancedHint: Optional policies and service settings. Values you do not change are preserved.
dialog.editor.saveNote: Device, service and access changes apply online. Changed services end their own connections; global listener settings still reload forwarding.
editor.allowClients: Allowed visitor nodes (comma separated, empty allows any authenticated node holding the key)
editor.allowConfigPush: Let the agent publish tunnels itself
editor.allowDirect: Allow P2P direct connections (the server and the serving agent must allow them too)
editor.allowDynamic: Allow a specified target (forward proxy tunnels with no separate account only)
editor.fileRootRequired: A file service needs file.root set under “More settings”, using a directory name the agent authorises.
editor.localsHint: Configure the local service's tunnel list and access rules.
editor.mode.direct: The platform connects to the node
editor.mode.reverse: The node connects to the platform
editor.name: Name
editor.shareClient: Node providing the service (use local.name for a local service)
editor.userAdminBlank: Owning user (leave empty for an administrator)
editor.userFullBlank: Owning user (leave empty for full access)
editor.consoleScope: Set the device's access range from the console
editor.consoleScopeHint: When off, the device uses the range in its own configuration file. When on, this range replaces it immediately; the device must allow it with remote.console_scope (packages from this console do).
error.badCredentials: The account or password is not correct.
error.configUpdating: The configuration is being updated. Refresh the data in a moment.
error.invalidJson: That is not valid JSON. Check the quotes, commas and brackets.
error.missingRevision: The configuration revision is missing. Refresh the page and try again.
error.notAnObject: The configuration must be a JSON object.
error.staleRevision: The configuration was updated by another operation. Close the editor, refresh the data and try again.
fatal.description: Reload the console. Anything you have not submitted is not saved.
fatal.title: This page cannot be shown right now
field.remote: Local resources available to the console
flow.advancedClientHint: Configure how a device connects, provides resources, and accesses remote services. Generate a file to apply on the device.
flow.allAuthenticated: All authenticated devices with the access secret
flow.bulkServicesHint: Configure a group of services or a range of ports on this device.
flow.connectHint: Name your device, then run the generated command on it to connect.
flow.connectionHelpText: Keep the client running. Check that the server address is reachable from this device and TCP port {port} is allowed. Check the client terminal for connection or certificate errors.
flow.copyManual: Select the address or command and copy it manually.
flow.devicesHint: Your connected computers and servers. Choose a device to manage its services.
flow.directHint: Try a direct connection first. If the network prevents it, traffic goes through your server automatically. Both devices must keep the client running.
flow.directServerHint: Allow UDP port {port} on your server to make direct connections possible. This page does not change firewall rules. Existing shares keep their current connection choice.
flow.domainHint: Leave empty to connect by server address. If set, point the domain to your server first.
flow.domainRequired: A website with domain routing needs a domain and public access.
flow.downloadFirst: Download and extract the package above, then open its start file on the target device.
flow.downloadHint: Use the felucca-agent client from the same release as your server. Put it and this file in the same folder on the device. The file is ready to use; do not edit it.
flow.existingLocalServices: This device already publishes services from its local file. Keep those services running; migrate them deliberately before adding services from this console.
flow.fileServiceHint: Uses the folder you authorized when connecting this device. New file services are read-only. If no folder was authorized, reconnect the device with a folder selected first.
flow.folderHint: Optional: an existing folder on this device, shared read-only. Leave empty to disable file sharing.
flow.hostInvalid: Enter a server hostname or IP address, without a URL or port.
flow.localAccessHint: Keep the receiving client running, then connect to this address from an application on that same device. A downloaded file does not mean the connection is already active.
flow.modeFixed: Create a new service to change its type. Existing service options have been preserved.
flow.packageBackground: Want to run automatically after sign-in? Close the current connection window first, then open {install} (on Linux: sh {install}). This saves the client to your personal directory and enables automatic startup. You can then delete the downloaded package.
flow.packageExists: This connection is already installed. Use the installed client.
flow.packageInstalled: Automatic startup is configured and the client is connecting.
flow.packageInstructions: Extract the download and open {connect} on the target device. The program and connection are included; no extra download or configuration editing is needed.
flow.packageLinuxInstructions: Extract the package and run {connect} inside its folder. The program and connection are included; no extra download or configuration editing is needed.
flow.packageSecret: The package contains this device’s access credentials. Use it only on the intended device and do not share it.
flow.packageStarting: Connecting {name}. Once connected, return to the console to continue. Closing this window disconnects the device.
flow.packageTargetHint: Choose the target device’s system and processor. Only matching client builds provided by this server are listed.
flow.packageUnavailable: The administrator has not provided client packages
flow.pendingPublish: Waiting for the device to apply
flow.permissionHint: Selected devices must also hold the connection file. An empty selection allows any authenticated device with the access secret. Removing a device here revokes its access to this service.
flow.privateFirst: First add a service and choose “Only connected devices”. Then authorize a receiving device here.
flow.privateHint: No public port is opened. Authorize a receiving device in Sharing to access this service.
flow.privateMode: Private access supports TCP, UDP and files. Use a public entry for this service type.
flow.proxyAuthRequired: Set an access username and password for this proxy.
flow.proxyHint: Set a username and password before exposing a proxy. Device permissions still limit which destinations it can reach.
flow.publicAccessHint: Allow port {port} on the server, then try this address from another network. The application behind this service still needs its own access controls.
flow.publicHint: People who can reach your server can connect to this port. The destination application's login still applies.
flow.publishedHint: Published means the device has registered the service. It does not prove that external access or the destination application is working.
flow.readyHint: Your device is online. Add the service you want to access next.
flow.receivingReconnect: This device receives a private service. Keep its original connection file, or create a new receiving device in Private access; a provider connection file would lose its local access settings.
flow.relayHint: This server currently relays connections. Enable direct connections in Settings to prefer a device-to-device path for new shares.
flow.removeDeviceHint: This device will lose access. Remove services and sharing rules that still refer to it first.
flow.removeServiceHint: This service will stop accepting connections. Remove its sharing rules first if it is shared.
flow.replaceConnection: This creates connection instructions for the same device without changing its identity. Check any local-network and folder permissions you previously granted before replacing the file.
flow.revokeHint: The receiving device will no longer be able to access this service.
flow.runHint: Open a terminal in that folder and run this command. Keep the client running.
flow.saveNote: Changes sync to the device automatically. Other services keep their connections.
flow.serverHostHint: Use the server's public IP or domain when connecting another computer. 127.0.0.1 only works on the server itself.
flow.serviceExample: For example: my NAS or home SSH
flow.serviceKind: What do you want to access?
flow.serviceSaved: Service saved. Its status shows whether the device has applied it.
flow.servicesHint: Choose a device and the application you want to access. Felucca connects it to the address you choose.
flow.settingsHint: Start with what you want to do. Defaults suit most uses; adjust connections, access, and operation when needed.
flow.shareFirst: Access a service from another device
flow.sharingHint: Choose a private service and prepare a client package for another device, without a public port.
flow.statusUnavailable: Status updates are unavailable; the last observed state is shown.
flow.syncFailed: Not applied: check device permissions or port conflicts
flow.takeOverHint: This device currently uses a local service list. Saving will switch it to console management. Check its existing services first and enable remote access in its connection instructions.
flow.targetHint: For example, 127.0.0.1:3000. This address is reached from the selected device. For another machine on its LAN, enable local-network access when connecting the device.
flow.targetInvalid: Enter the application's address and port, for example 127.0.0.1:3000.
flow.waitingHint: Open the start file in the package. This page checks automatically when the device comes online.
flow.websiteAdmin: Ask an administrator to enable the first website entry on the server.
login.consoleDescription: Manage devices, services and access permissions. Inspect service status.
login.panelMuted: Sign in with a management account.
monitor.adminOnly: Host CPU, memory, disk and network data is for administrators only.
monitor.caption.hints: Hover to inspect · click to pin · drag the range bar to zoom · arrow keys step through samples
monitor.caption.timezone: Times use the browser's local timezone
monitor.chart.cpu.description: Whole-machine CPU usage · all logical cores
monitor.chart.disk.description: The file system the service runs on · capacity usage
monitor.chart.network.description: All non-loopback interfaces · average rate between neighbouring samples
monitor.description: Connections and total traffic for the resources this account can see.
monitor.hostDescription: How the host is behaving and where its resources are heading, updated continuously.
monitor.profileDownloaded: The CPU flame graph was downloaded.
monitor.staleData: Sampling has not updated yet; the chart shows the last data received.
monitor.trafficDescription: Connections and total traffic at the moment the page loaded, shown according to your account's permissions.
monitor.updateFailed: Cannot update right now: {error}. The last data received is kept and the read retries automatically.
nav.accounts.description: Manage sign-in accounts, roles and user scopes.
nav.clients.description: Your connected computers and servers. Choose a device to manage its services.
nav.config.description: Validate, import and manage the whole server configuration.
nav.locals.description: Publish services running on the server itself.
nav.monitor.description: Inspect host metrics, connection counts and cumulative traffic.
nav.node.description: Manage platform links, event delivery and configuration changes.
nav.platforms.description: Configure credentials, connection modes and permissions for external management platforms.
nav.shares.description: Choose a private service and generate a connection file for another device. No public service port is needed.
nav.tunnels.description: Choose a device and the application you want to access. Felucca connects it to the address you choose.
nav.users.description: Organise resources by user, with quotas and access rules.
nav.webhooks.description: Configure event endpoints, signing secrets and delivery rules.
notice.callbacksReplayed: The selected events were queued again.
notice.nodeConfigUpdated: The node's configuration method was updated.
overview.description: Device, service and connection status visible to this account.
overview.emptyHint: Connect a device to start publishing services.
overview.healthCheckBlurb: The forwarding service is unavailable. Check the service logs.
overview.totalTrafficHint: Total traffic for the resources this account can see
peer.setup_failed: Direct setup failed or timed out
platform.callbacksDescription: See the subscription queues and how event delivery is going.
platform.changesDescription: The configuration change events on record.
platform.deleteCallbacksMessage: These delivery records will be removed from the failure queue.
platform.disabled.description: The platform node identity (node.id and node.state_path) is not configured. An administrator must configure it offline and restart the service; it cannot be enabled here.
platform.disabled.title: Platform connections disabled
platform.emptyDescription: Add a connection configuration in the management platform.
platform.journalError: Writing the node state failed. Check the service log.
platform.noPendingDescription: New delivery records will show up here.
platform.noPendingTitle: No pending or failed events on this page.
platform.resyncMessage: Forward connections break and the agent reconnects; the configuration and traffic stay on the host.
resources.deleteMessage: Deleting it interrupts the matching service. The operation is refused while a related user or account still references it.
status.configChanged: The configuration changed. Refresh to see the latest data.
status.configReconnecting: Configuration notifications disconnected. Reconnecting; refresh data manually to check for changes.
table.name: Name
tunnels.centralEnabledHint: Centralized configuration is enabled. Add a tunnel and set its backend address.
tunnels.connectFirstDescription: Add a node before configuring tunnels.
tunnels.deleteMessage: Deleting it interrupts the service this tunnel serves.
tunnels.emptyPublishedDescription: Publish a service on the agent, or turn on central configuration.
tunnels.enableCentralMessage: The tunnels this agent reports will stop. Make sure the agent allows remote configuration first, then create tunnels here.
tunnels.localInfo: This node publishes tunnels from its agent's local configuration. With central configuration on, the console's configuration wins; the agent needs remote.enabled, plus the allowed targets and file directories.
tunnels.restoreLocalMessage: Central configuration will be removed and the agent will publish the local configuration it started with.
tunnels.waitingForNode: Waiting for the node to apply it
flow.packageMacUnverified: This macOS build has not been notarized by Apple and may be blocked at first launch. Ask the server administrator for a release build.
flow.visitorLan: Allow other devices on this network to use the entry
flow.visitorLanHint: Listens on 0.0.0.0 instead of 127.0.0.1, so other computers on the receiving device's network can connect.
flow.launchCommandHint: Run this in the folder that holds felucca-agent. Services and the access range then come from this console; nothing else is stored on the device. The command contains the device key, so treat it like a password.
guide.unset: Using the default behavior; no value needed
guide.agentApply: This is a new configuration draft, not the device’s running settings. Export it and load it on the selected device to apply it.
guide.start.title: What would you like to do?
guide.start.description: Use a wizard to connect a device or access a shared service. No advanced setup is needed first.
guide.group.accessHint: Manage service users, console accounts, and services provided by the server itself.
guide.group.maintenanceHint: Run diagnostics first if a connection fails. Change configuration only when you need different behavior.
guide.group.integrationsHint: Configure these only for external management platforms or automated notifications.
guide.connection.title: Connect to a server
guide.connection.description: The server identifies this device and coordinates its service connections.
guide.connection.when: Change this when moving servers or creating a connection file manually. For a first connection, use the Connect device wizard.
guide.remote.title: Which device resources can the console use?
guide.remote.description: When this device provides services, its local configuration limits the addresses and folders they can access. Services sent by the console must stay within those limits.
guide.remote.when: Adjust this to publish local apps, LAN services, or folders through the console.
guide.remote.off: Service configuration from the console is not accepted
guide.remote.local: Only 127.0.0.1 is allowed; no folders are authorized
guide.remote.files: Folders are specified; see address limits below
guide.remote.custom: Custom address limits; no folders are authorized
guide.remote.unrestricted: No target address or port limits; no folders are authorized
guide.remote.impact: Network destinations are unrestricted by default. Advanced settings can limit addresses, domains or ports. Authorize folders individually; new folders start read-only.
guide.visitor.title: Access remote services from this device
guide.visitor.description: Create a local entry for a service you are authorized to use. Browsers and database tools can then connect as if the service were local.
guide.visitor.when: Use this to access a private service shared with you. Generate an access package from the sharing page.
guide.visitor.current: This configuration has {count} local access entries
guide.visitor.example: For example, an app connecting to 127.0.0.1:18080 can reach the shared service. Only this device can use that entry.
guide.visitor.add: Add an entry from an existing share
guide.directAgent.title: Let this device send service data directly
guide.directAgent.description: Device-to-device connections (P2P) carry service data between two devices, reducing server relay traffic. The server still authenticates and coordinates connections.
guide.directAgent.when: Enable when services on this device need direct connections and both the server and the share permissions allow them.
guide.directAgent.on: Direct service connections are allowed, subject to share permissions
guide.directAgent.off: Direct service connections are off; server relay remains available
guide.directAgent.impact: This does not change existing shares. Access entries set to prefer direct connections try relay if direct fails; direct-only entries do not.
guide.time.title: Time used to verify connections
guide.time.description: Felucca needs accurate time to verify connections. It normally uses the device’s system time, without a separate time server (NTP).
guide.time.when: Adjust if connection errors mention clock differences or an internal time server is required. Check system automatic time settings first.
guide.time.systemState: Using system time; no separate setup needed
guide.time.customState: A custom time server calibrates connection verification time
guide.time.systemHint: Let the operating system keep time; suitable for most devices.
guide.time.customHint: Enter a reachable NTP address to calibrate Felucca connection verification only.
guide.time.impact: This does not change the computer’s clock or certificate verification time. If the time server is unavailable and no valid calibration remains, Felucca uses system time.
guide.network.title: Adapt to a special network environment
guide.network.description: Choose a network interface, DNS, or upstream proxy and tune reconnection. Defaults usually work.
guide.network.when: Adjust for multiple network interfaces, a required company proxy, or connection issues you have already diagnosed.
guide.directServer.title: How devices transfer data
guide.directServer.description: Server relay needs the least setup and is the default. You can also enable device-to-device connections (P2P) to reduce server traffic.
guide.directServer.when: Consider enabling direct connections for frequent large transfers or to reduce server bandwidth use.
guide.directServer.on: Direct support is enabled; each share determines its connection mode
guide.directServer.relayHint: Devices only need the server connection; no additional direct connection port is required.
guide.directServer.directHint: Provide a server address and UDP port reachable by devices, then choose the connection mode for each share.
guide.directServer.portHint: This UDP port coordinates direct connections; it is not the application’s port.
guide.directServer.impact: Saving reloads forwarding and may briefly interrupt connections. Existing shares keep their connection mode. Before disabling, check for direct-only access entries.
guide.directServer.confirmOn: Saving direct connection settings reloads forwarding and may briefly interrupt connections. Existing share modes will not change automatically.
guide.directServer.confirmOff: Disabling prevents direct-only entries from working. Entries that prefer direct can try server relay. Saving reloads forwarding and may briefly interrupt connections.
guide.server.bridge.title: Device connections to the server
guide.server.bridge.description: Set the entry where the server accepts devices. All devices use this address and port.
guide.server.bridge.when: Change when migrating servers, changing the device port, or updating connection certificates.
guide.server.bridge.default: The default device port is 14028. Update device connection addresses if it changes. Validation checks whether a restart is needed.
guide.server.http.title: Access websites by domain
guide.server.http.description: Share HTTP/HTTPS entries across domains and configure website certificates.
guide.server.http.when: Configure to publish websites by domain. TCP/UDP port services do not require it.
guide.server.http.default: Without configuration, domain web entries are off. Address or certificate changes may require reload or restart as indicated by validation.
guide.server.allowed_ports.title: Server ports available to services
guide.server.allowed_ports.description: Limit ports used to publish services and avoid conflicts with other apps.
guide.server.allowed_ports.when: Adjust on shared servers or when reserving ports for other apps.
guide.server.allowed_ports.default: An empty list allows ports above 1024. A populated list allows only its ports and ranges.
guide.server.acl_mode.title: How access rules work
guide.server.acl_mode.description: Choose whether global rules block matching visitors or allow only matching visitors.
guide.server.acl_mode.when: Adjust for global source restrictions, together with access rules.
guide.server.acl_mode.default: The default blocks matches. Empty rules add no restriction at this layer. Allow-only mode requires rules; user and service restrictions still apply.
guide.server.acl_rules.title: Sources to allow or block
guide.server.acl_rules.description: Match visitor IPs or networks, then apply the selected access-rule mode.
guide.server.acl_rules.when: Use to allow office access only or block known sources.
guide.server.acl_rules.default: For example, ip:192.168.1.0/24 matches that network. Check the rule mode first. Geographic rules also require a location database.
guide.server.geo.title: Identify sources by region or site
guide.server.geo.description: Supply data files used by geographic and site rules.
guide.server.geo.when: Needed only for geographic or site matching, not ordinary IP rules.
guide.server.geo.default: No databases are loaded by default. Paths must be readable on the server.
guide.server.ntp.title: Time used to verify connections
guide.server.state.title: Keep traffic usage after restart
guide.server.state.description: Periodically save traffic usage to disk so totals survive restarts.
guide.server.state.when: Enable to preserve cumulative user or service usage.
guide.server.state.default: Without configuration, usage is in memory and is lost on restart. This is separate from console configuration storage.
guide.server.log.title: Record activity and errors
guide.server.log.description: Choose log detail and whether to write to a file or process output.
guide.server.log.when: Adjust when troubleshooting connections or retaining logs long-term.
guide.server.log.default: The default records info and more severe events to process output unless a file is specified. Debug/trace produce more data; restore the level after troubleshooting.
guide.server.admin.title: Where the console is accessible
guide.server.admin.description: Set this console’s listening address, sessions, and configuration storage.
guide.server.admin.when: Change when moving the console, placing it behind a reverse proxy, or adjusting session lifetime.
guide.server.admin.default: Disabling the console or using a wrong address can make this page unreachable. Confirm the new address and follow validation results.
guide.server.node.title: Accept external platform management
guide.server.node.description: Let an external platform manage this server through the node API. This is separate from ordinary device connections.
guide.server.node.when: Use when integrating with an existing external node-management platform.
guide.server.node.default: Off by default and unnecessary for ordinary device connections. Requires the admin console to be configured.
guide.field.server.label: Server connection address
guide.field.server.hint: The server host and port this device connects to, for example example.com:14028.
guide.field.deviceIdentity.label: Device identity
guide.field.deviceIdentity.hint: Must match the registered device. Set its display name in the connection wizard.
guide.field.deviceSecret.label: Device connection key
guide.field.deviceSecret.hint: Proves this device’s identity and must match the console. Use Fill credentials to retrieve it.
guide.field.transport.label: Device connection protocol
guide.field.transport.hint: How the device connects to the server. TLS is the default; change only for network requirements.
guide.field.trust.label: Server identity verification
guide.field.trust.hint: Use trusted certificates or a pinned fingerprint to prevent server impersonation.
guide.field.remoteEnabled.label: Accept service configuration from the console
guide.field.remoteEnabled.hint: Still limited by the address and folder rules below. Off when not configured.
guide.field.targets.label: Addresses services may access
guide.field.targets.hint: Limit destinations reached through this device, such as local apps or a specific LAN.
guide.field.folders.label: Folders allowed for sharing
guide.field.folders.hint: Each entry maps an alias to a local folder. An empty list authorizes no folders.
guide.field.allow.label: Allowed destinations
guide.field.allow.hint: For example, ip:127.0.0.1/32 allows only localhost. An empty list does not narrow destinations; deny and port rules still apply.
guide.field.deny.label: Blocked destinations
guide.field.deny.hint: Matching addresses are denied even if the allow list includes them.
guide.field.targetPorts.label: Destination ports
guide.field.targetPorts.hint: Empty adds no port limit. Otherwise only listed destination ports are allowed.
guide.field.folderPath.label: Folder path on the device
guide.field.folderPath.hint: An existing folder on the computer running the agent, not on the server.
guide.field.readOnly.label: Read-only access
guide.field.readOnly.hint: On by default. Disabling may let people with the relevant service permissions modify files.
guide.field.entryName.label: Local entry name
guide.field.entryName.hint: Distinguishes entries. Use letters, digits, dots, hyphens, and underscores.
guide.field.share.label: Share to use
guide.field.share.hint: Must match an existing share authorization. The wizard fills this for you.
guide.field.shareSecret.label: Share access key
guide.field.shareSecret.hint: Provided by the owner and must match this share. It is separate from the device connection key.
guide.field.visitorBind.label: Local address for your app
guide.field.visitorBind.hint: 127.0.0.1:18080 is local-only. Binding to 0.0.0.0 also lets LAN devices connect to this entry.
guide.field.connectionMode.label: How this entry reaches the service
guide.field.connectionMode.hint: Relay is the default. Prefer direct falls back to relay; direct-only fails if unavailable. Share permissions must allow the mode.
guide.field.visitorTarget.label: Target for a dynamic service
guide.field.visitorTarget.hint: Only needed for dynamic shares. Fixed services usually leave this unset; SOCKS5 gets the target from the app request.
guide.field.visitorMode.label: Local entry type
guide.field.visitorMode.hint: Usually TCP. Use UDP or SOCKS5 only when required by the app or share.
guide.field.directEnabled.label: Allow this device to provide direct services
guide.field.directEnabled.hint: Off by default. The server and the relevant share must also allow direct connections.
guide.field.directIp.label: Local IP for direct connections
guide.field.directIp.hint: Chosen automatically when unset. Specify an existing local IP only for special network setups.
guide.field.directLimit.label: Maximum concurrent direct sessions
guide.field.directLimit.hint: The default is 64. Lowering saves resources but can limit direct connection availability.
guide.field.timeServer.label: Time server address
guide.field.timeServer.hint: Host or IP and UDP port, for example time.example.com:123. This is not the Felucca server address.
guide.field.timeInterval.label: Calibration interval
guide.field.timeInterval.hint: Every 5 minutes by default. Use durations such as 5m or 1h.
guide.field.timeTimeout.label: Calibration timeout
guide.field.timeTimeout.hint: 5 seconds by default. Must be shorter than the interval and no more than 30 seconds.
guide.field.timeOffset.label: Maximum accepted clock difference
guide.field.timeOffset.hint: 24 hours by default. Larger corrections are rejected; check system time first.
guide.field.sourceIp.label: Local IP for server connections
guide.field.sourceIp.hint: The system chooses an interface by default. A specified IP must exist on this device.
guide.field.dns.label: DNS servers
guide.field.dns.hint: Uses system DNS by default. Specify for internal company domains or special networks.
guide.field.proxy.label: Upstream proxy for server connections
guide.field.proxy.hint: Used by TCP, TLS, WS, and WSS. QUIC/KCP and service backend connections do not use this proxy.
guide.field.forwardIp.label: Use the specified local IP for backends too
guide.field.forwardIp.hint: Enable only with a local IP configured. Otherwise the system selects the backend interface.
guide.field.bridgeBind.label: Device connection listener
guide.field.bridgeBind.hint: Default: 0.0.0.0:14028, on all IPv4 interfaces. Separate from application and console ports.
guide.field.strictClock.label: Check device/server clock differences
guide.field.strictClock.hint: Off by default. Inaccurate device clocks may cause rejection when enabled; check automatic time synchronization first.
guide.field.bridgeTls.label: Server certificate for device connections
guide.field.bridgeTls.hint: When unset, an automatic self-signed certificate can be used. Devices with pinned fingerprints need updates after certificate changes.
guide.field.consoleScope.hint: Lets the device editor in the console replace the range below. The device must still keep remote configuration on.
guide.field.consoleScope.label: Let the console set the access range
guide.remote.lan: Local addresses and private networks; no folders shared
option.prefer_direct: Prefer direct, fall back to relay
scope.denyHint: Matches are refused even when allowed above. Leave empty for none.
scope.empty: Add at least one rule, or choose another option.
scope.portsHint: For example 80, 443. Leave empty to allow any port.
scope.rulesHint: For example 192.168.1.0/24, 10.0.0.5, nas.local or *.corp.example. Commas also separate rules.
scope.source.anyHint: Anyone who can reach the entry.
scope.source.customHint: Allow or block the addresses you list.
scope.source.deviceHint: Only loopback addresses on the entry host: 127.0.0.1 and ::1.
scope.source.lanHint: Only this machine and private networks.
scope.sourceRulesHint: For example 203.0.113.0/24 or 192.168.1.10. Commas also separate rules.
scope.target.anyHint: Allow all networks by default, including this device, the LAN and the Internet.
scope.target.customHint: List addresses, networks or domains, one per line.
scope.target.lanHint: Also services on private networks this device reaches: 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, fc00::/7.
scope.trusted.customHint: List load balancer addresses or networks.
scope.trusted.deviceHint: A load balancer on this machine.
field.allow_config_push: Let the agent publish tunnels itself
field.allow_clients: Allowed visitor nodes (comma separated, empty allows any authenticated node holding the key)
field.connection: How this entry reaches the service
field.console_scope: Let the console set the access range
field.forward_local_ip: Use the specified local IP for backends too
field.geo: Identify sources by region or site
field.name: Name
field.backend_http2: Use HTTP/2 to connect to destinations
form.group.accessHint: Limit who can connect and which destinations services may reach.
form.group.advancedHint: Change these only when you need the corresponding capability. Existing values are preserved.
form.group.securityHint: Configure certificates used to authenticate and encrypt connections.
form.group.routingHint: Adjust domain routing, request handling, and response headers.
form.defaultHint: Not overridden. Skip this if no change is needed.
form.durationHint: Include a time unit: s for seconds, m for minutes, h for hours.
form.invalid: Check the format of this value.
form.portsInvalid: Use ports from 1 to 65535, separated by commas. For example: 80, 443.
form.destinationExceptions: Exclude addresses or restrict destination ports
option.source_hash: Keep the same destination per source
form.hint.services: Add the services this device provides. Open a service to edit its addresses and access rules.
form.hint.mappings: Forward several ports in order. Use an individual service for a single application.
form.hint.deviceTargets: Limit the addresses services on this device may reach. This does not select who can connect.
form.hint.serviceName: Use a recognizable name, such as Office website or Home NAS.
form.hint.serviceMode: Choose the protocol used by the application you want to publish.
form.hint.public: When enabled, connections can enter through the server. When disabled, use private access.
form.hint.enabled: Disable to stop this service; keep its settings for later use.
form.hint.serviceId: Used to identify an existing service. Usually you do not need to change it.
form.hint.publicPort: The port visitors connect to on the server, not the application's own port.
form.hint.publicBind: Select which server network interface accepts connections. Unset means all interfaces.
form.hint.hosts: For HTTP routing, enter one domain per row, such as app.example.com.
form.hint.backends: Where this device forwards traffic. Add more than one address only for multiple application instances.
form.hint.backendAddress: Use host:port as reachable from the device, for example 127.0.0.1:3000.
form.hint.weight: Used by weighted balancing. A larger number receives a larger share of connections.
form.hint.backendTls: Enable when the destination application itself uses TLS, such as HTTPS.
form.hint.trust: Choose how to verify the destination's certificate.
form.hint.file: Only used by file services. Configure the authorized folder and access behavior.
form.hint.folder: Use an authorized folder name for device services, or an existing path for server-local services.
form.hint.prefix: The URL path that exposes the folder. Use / for the website root.
form.hint.readOnly: When enabled, visitors cannot upload, overwrite, or delete files.
form.hint.autoIndex: Show the folder's file list when there is no index page.
form.hint.balance: Choose how connections are distributed when several destinations are configured.
form.hint.health: Periodically check destinations and temporarily exclude those that fail.
form.hint.healthType: TCP checks whether a connection opens; HTTP also checks the response.
form.hint.healthPath: For HTTP checks, use a path such as /health. Default: /.
form.hint.statusCodes: Leave the list empty to accept any HTTP 2xx response.
form.hint.serviceTargets: Restrict this service's destinations. Device authorization still applies.
form.hint.routeOptions: Optional authentication, protocol, and forwarding behavior.
form.hint.mappingMode: Choose TCP or UDP to match the applications behind these ports.
form.hint.serverPorts: Ports visitors connect to, for example 8000-8002.
form.hint.targetPorts: Use the same number of ports as the server ports. They are matched in order.
form.hint.targetHost: Host reachable from the device. Do not include a port here.
form.hint.cert: Path to the PEM certificate on the server.
form.hint.key: Path to the matching private key on the server.
option.reverse: The node connects to the platform
connect.commandHint: Copy this command into the terminal on the device you want to connect. It downloads and verifies the matching client, saves the connection, and starts it.
connect.keepRunning: Keep this window open. Network interruptions reconnect automatically; run the same command to connect again after closing it.
connect.shareCommand: You can give this command to the device owner. It grants access as this device, so keep it private.
connect.runCommand: Run the command above on the device. This page will show when it connects.
connect.desktopHint: Using the Felucca desktop app on this computer? It keeps the connection in the tray after you close the window.
